name: Jorethang
tagline: The Rangeet river town where South and West Sikkim change jeeps
meta_description: Jorethang, South Sikkim: the Rangeet junction for Darjeeling, Namchi and Pelling, the January Maghe Sankranti Mela, bazaar food and 2026 jeep fares.
summary: Jorethang is a warm market town at about 320 m on the Rangeet river, ≈ 30 km from Darjeeling and ≈ 17 km below Namchi. Most travellers pass through to change jeeps for Pelling or Namchi. Stop for the morning bazaar, the riverside, a day hop to Legship, or the Maghe Sankranti Mela in mid-January.
intro: Jorethang sits at about 320 m on the bank of the Rangeet, a tributary of the Teesta, where the river runs between Sikkim and Darjeeling district. It is the lowest and warmest town most visitors see in Sikkim. At the 2011 census it had 9,009 people, and it works as a junction: roads lead up to Namchi, out to Legship, Gyalshing and Pelling, west towards Soreng and Okhrey, and across the river to Darjeeling, ≈ 30 km and 1.5–2 hours away.

Most travellers know Jorethang only as the place where the jeep stops. Shared jeeps from Darjeeling arrive here for about ₹150–200 a seat, and onward jeeps to Gyalshing and Pelling cost about ₹150–250, indicative, 2026. Most onward jeeps leave before about 1 pm, so if you arrive late you may be spending the night. That is not a bad thing. Jorethang has a busy market, cheap food and a riverside that is pleasant in the cool months.

We suggest treating Jorethang as a useful stop rather than a destination, unless your dates match the Maghe Sankranti Mela in mid-January, when the town hosts a week-long fair on the Rangeet. Namchi is ≈ 17 km and 40 minutes uphill, Okhrey about 2 hours away, and the Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple at Legship is an easy day hop. From April to September Jorethang is hot and humid, so most people pass through quickly in those months.

story.title: A river town and its January fair
paras: Jorethang grew where roads meet a river. The Rangeet comes down from West Sikkim and the Singalila side, and at Jorethang it is wide enough, and the valley low enough, for a market town to sit on its bank. Traders from Darjeeling, Namchi and the villages of the west met here, and they still do. Wikivoyage calls it a common night halt for travellers heading to Pelling, Darjeeling and Siliguri, which is how most visitors meet it today.

Once a year the town becomes a destination in its own right. Maghe Sankranti falls on the first day of the month of Magh in the Nepali calendar, around 14 January, when the sun enters Makara, or Capricorn. It marks the turn from the coldest days towards longer, warmer ones. Nepali Hindu families bathe in rivers, visit relatives and eat festive foods such as chaku, ghee and sweet potatoes, and in the hills sel roti is fried at home for the day.

At Jorethang the day is marked by a week-long mela on the banks of the Rangeet. Sikkim government notices put the 71st Maghe Sankranti Mela at 14–22 January 2026, which shows how long the fair has run. Expect stalls, food, crowds and evening programmes, and plenty of families from nearby villages in their best clothes. If you are passing in mid-January, plan a night here, and check current status before you travel, as dates are confirmed each year.

did_you_know: At the 2011 census Jorethang had 9,009 residents, and Nepali was the most common language, followed by Hindi.
The Rangeet, which flows past Jorethang, is a tributary of the Teesta, joining it downstream near the West Bengal border.
The Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple at Legship, up the Rangeet from Jorethang, holds its biggest gatherings at Bala Chaturdashi in November–December and Maha Shivaratri in February–March.
facts: Jeep junction, Maghe Sankranti Mela, Rangeet river

highlights.title: Maghe Sankranti Mela in January
highlights.text: Around 14 January Jorethang hosts a week-long fair on the Rangeet for Maghe Sankranti; the 71st mela ran from 14 to 22 January 2026. Expect food stalls, crowds and evening programmes. Book a room early and check current status before you travel.

highlights.title: The junction that saves you money
highlights.text: Shared jeeps from Darjeeling to Jorethang cost about ₹150–200 a seat, and on to Pelling or Gyalshing about ₹150–250, indicative, 2026. That is a fraction of a reserved car. Arrive by late morning, since most onward jeeps leave before about 1 pm.

highlights.title: Morning bazaar and bazaar food
highlights.text: The market is busiest in the morning, with vegetables from the villages, river-valley fruit in season, and stalls frying sel roti and serving tea. Look for dried chhurpi, the hard local cheese, and fermented foods such as gundruk and kinema to take home.

highlights.title: Evening on the Rangeet
highlights.text: At about 320 m, Jorethang is warm even in winter. Walk down to the riverbank in the late afternoon, when the light is soft and the heat has gone. Watch the current from a safe distance; the Rangeet runs fast and cold, and it is not for swimming.

highlights.title: Day hop to Namchi or Legship
highlights.text: Namchi's Samdruptse and Char Dham are ≈ 17 km and 40 minutes uphill, and the Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple at Legship lies up the Rangeet road, about an hour away. Either makes an easy half day from Jorethang by shared jeep or local taxi.

how_to_reach.text: From Darjeeling, shared jeeps run to Jorethang for about ₹150–200 a seat, ≈ 30 km and 1.5–2 hours. From Siliguri, jeeps for Gyalshing and Pelling pass through Jorethang, and there are direct Jorethang jeeps too; expect to pay a little less than the ₹400–550 Pelling fare. Jorethang to Namchi is about 40 minutes. All fares indicative, 2026; check current status before you travel.

Most reserved cars from Darjeeling to Pelling, about ₹4,000–5,500 one way, indicative, 2026, run through Jorethang, so ask your driver for a stop at the bazaar or the river. From Siliguri the drive takes about 3–3.5 hours. A local taxi to Namchi or Legship is easy to arrange at the stand.
New Jalpaiguri (NJP) is the nearest major station, about 3–3.5 hours away by road. Take an auto to the Siliguri jeep stands for a shared seat, or book a car at the station.

Bagdogra (IXB) is ≈ 110 km away and has the most flights. Allow at least 3.5 hours by road from the airport, longer in the monsoon when the Teesta valley road is prone to landslides; check current status before you travel.

where_to_stay: Jorethang has a handful of simple hotels and lodges in the bazaar and near the jeep stand, used mostly by travellers who miss the last onward jeep and by traders. They are basic but cheap, and fine for one night; look at the room and check the fan or heater and hot water before you pay. Rooms are scarce during the Maghe Sankranti Mela in January, so book ahead. For a more comfortable night, go on to Namchi, ≈ 17 km uphill, which has a wider choice of hotels, or to Okhrey, about 2 hours away, for Sherpa family homestays. We do not list a named Jorethang hotel because none we know well enough to recommend.
costs: Shared jeep Jorethang → Gyalshing or Pelling
Reserved car Darjeeling → Pelling via Jorethang
budget_tip: Travel Darjeeling to Pelling in two shared-jeep legs via Jorethang, about ₹300–450 a seat in total, indicative, instead of a ₹4,000–5,500 reserved car, and leave Darjeeling by 8 am to catch an onward jeep before about 1 pm.
tips: Reach Jorethang by late morning if you are changing jeeps; most onward jeeps to Pelling and Gyalshing leave before about 1 pm.
Pack light clothes for Jorethang and warm ones for where you are going; it can be 10 °C warmer here than in Pelling.
Foreign nationals should arrange the Sikkim Restricted Area Permit online through e-FRRO before arriving; check current status before you travel.
Do not swim or wade in the Rangeet; the current is fast and water levels change quickly, especially in the monsoon.
Carry cash; ATMs exist, but queues and outages are common on market and mela days.

experiences.title: Maghe Sankranti Mela on the Rangeet
experiences.duration: Half day to a full evening
experiences.best_time: Around 14 January, for about a week
experiences.cost: Free entry; budget ₹300–800 for food and rides, indicative
experiences.summary: For about a week from the first of Magh, around 14 January, Jorethang hosts a fair on the banks of the Rangeet for Maghe Sankranti. The 71st mela ran from 14 to 22 January 2026. Come for food, stalls, evening programmes and a crowd that is almost entirely local.
body: Maghe Sankranti falls on the first day of Magh in the Nepali calendar, around 14 January, when the sun enters Makara, or Capricorn. It marks the turn from the coldest part of winter towards longer, warmer days. Nepali Hindu families take ritual baths in rivers, visit relatives and share festive food, and Wikipedia notes that Buddhists and Kirati communities also join in. In the hills, sel roti is a fixture of the day.

At Jorethang the festival grows into a week-long mela on the Rangeet. Sikkim government notices put the 71st edition at 14–22 January 2026. Expect lines of stalls selling clothes, household goods and snacks, rides for children, and evening cultural programmes on a stage. The crowd is mostly local families from Jorethang and the villages around, and the mood is relaxed and friendly. Evenings are cool at the river, so bring a jacket.

Entry to the grounds is usually free or nominal; budget about ₹300–800 per person for food, rides and small shopping, indicative, 2026. Rooms in Jorethang are scarce during the mela, so book ahead or stay in Namchi and come down by taxi. Watch your phone and wallet in the crowd. Dates and programmes are confirmed each year, so check current status before you travel. Shared jeeps run as usual during the mela, but expect slower traffic around the bridge and bazaar in the evenings.

faqs.q: When is the Maghe Sankranti Mela in Jorethang
faqs.a: The mela starts on Maghe Sankranti, the first of Magh, which usually falls on 14 January, and runs for about a week. In 2026 the 71st Maghe Sankranti Mela ran from 14 to 22 January, according to the Sikkim government. Dates are confirmed every year, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Jorethang mela worth a special trip
faqs.a: It is worth a night if you are already in Darjeeling, Namchi or West Sikkim in mid-January. It is a local fair, not a staged show, with food, stalls, rides and evening programmes on the Rangeet. Combine it with Namchi or Pelling rather than travelling far just for the mela.

faqs.q: What food is eaten at Maghe Sankranti
faqs.a: Wikipedia lists chaku, a hard molasses sweet, ghee and sweet potatoes among the traditional foods, and in Sikkim and Darjeeling families also fry sel roti, a ring-shaped rice bread. At the Jorethang mela you will find stalls selling these alongside momos, chow mein and tea. Try the sel roti fresh and hot.

experiences.title: Morning bazaar, sel roti and chhurpi
experiences.cost: ₹150–400 per person for snacks and tea, indicative
experiences.summary: Jorethang's market is busiest in the morning, when villages bring in vegetables and stalls fry sel roti and pour tea. Walk it slowly, eat as you go and buy hill staples such as dried chhurpi, gundruk and kinema to carry home. It is cheap, filling and very local.
body: Jorethang is a trading town, and the market shows it. Mornings are best, when villagers come down with vegetables, greens and seasonal fruit from the warmer river valley, and shops open their shutters for the day. Start with tea at a stall and a sel roti, the ring-shaped, slightly sweet rice bread fried in oil that Nepali households make for festivals and that many tea shops sell every day. Eat it hot, with sweet milky tea or a spicy potato curry, the way locals do.

Look out for chhurpi in two forms: soft, fresh cheese used in curries and pickles, and the hard, dried blocks that people chew for an hour or more. Gundruk, fermented and dried leafy greens, and kinema, fermented soybean, are hill staples with a strong smell and a strong following. Momos and thukpa are easy to find for lunch, as are simple rice-and-dal thalis for about ₹150–350, indicative, 2026. Ask the stall owner what is fresh that day; the answer is usually the best thing on the menu.

Ask before photographing sellers, carry small notes and bring your own cloth bag. Hard chhurpi and dried gundruk travel well; soft cheese does not. Choose busy stalls, eat food that is cooked in front of you and drink bottled or filtered water. A slow walk through the bazaar takes one to two hours and costs very little, and it is a good way to fill the wait for an onward jeep.

faqs.q: What is sel roti
faqs.a: Sel roti is a ring-shaped, slightly sweet bread made from a rice batter and deep-fried in oil. Nepali households in Sikkim and Darjeeling make it for festivals such as Tihar and Maghe Sankranti, and many tea stalls sell it every morning. It is best eaten hot with tea or a spicy potato curry.

faqs.q: What is chhurpi and can I carry it home
faqs.a: Chhurpi is a traditional cheese of the eastern Himalaya. The soft kind goes into curries and pickles, while the hard, dried kind is chewed slowly like a sweet and lasts for months. Hard chhurpi travels very well in a sealed bag, so it makes a cheap, easy food souvenir from Jorethang.

faqs.q: Is street food in Jorethang safe to eat
faqs.a: Generally yes, if you choose sensibly. Eat at busy stalls, pick food that is cooked or fried in front of you and served hot, and avoid raw salads and cut fruit left in the open. Drink bottled or filtered water. Carry basic stomach medicine if you are sensitive to spice or oil.

experiences.title: Evening walk along the Rangeet
experiences.summary: At about 320 m, Jorethang is warm when the hills are cold. In the late afternoon, walk down to the Rangeet, a fast, green-grey tributary of the Teesta, and watch the light go off the valley sides. It is free, quiet and a good break on a long jeep day.
body: The Rangeet rises in West Sikkim and runs south past Legship and Jorethang before joining the Teesta near the West Bengal border. At Jorethang it is a wide, fast river between steep, forested slopes, with Darjeeling district on the far bank. In the cool months the water is clear and green-grey; in the monsoon it turns brown and loud. The town sits at about 320 m, so evenings here are mild when Pelling is close to freezing.

Walk down from the bazaar towards the riverbank in the late afternoon. You will see families out for a stroll, children playing on the open ground and, in January, the mela site taking shape. Birds work the river edge, and the light goes golden on the slopes opposite before the valley falls into shade. It is a simple hour, and a good way to stretch after a long jeep ride.

Stay well back from the water. The Rangeet is fast and cold, levels can rise without warning when dams upstream release water or rain falls in the hills, and the rocks are slippery. Do not swim or wade, and keep children close. From June to September keep away from the bank entirely and check current status before you travel, as roads along the river are prone to landslides. In the dry months, a torch is useful for the walk back up to the bazaar after dark.

faqs.q: Can you swim in the Rangeet at Jorethang
faqs.a: No, we strongly advise against it. The Rangeet is fast and cold, the rocks are slippery, and water levels can rise quickly with rain in the hills or releases from dams upstream. Enjoy the river from the bank, keep children close and stay well away from the water from June to September.

faqs.q: Where does the Rangeet river flow
faqs.a: The Rangeet rises in West Sikkim and flows south past Legship and Jorethang, forming part of the border between Sikkim and Darjeeling district, before joining the Teesta near the West Bengal border. It is the main river of West and South Sikkim and the reason many of the region's market towns grew where they did.

faqs.q: What is the best time for a riverside walk in Jorethang
faqs.a: Late afternoon from October to March is best, when the heat has gone, the light is soft and the water is clear. Jorethang sits at about 320 m, so it stays mild even in winter. From April to September it is hot, humid and often wet, and the river runs high and muddy.

experiences.title: Day hop to Kirateshwar Mahadev at Legship
experiences.best_time: Mornings, Oct–Mar; Maha Shivaratri and Bala Chaturdashi for festivals
experiences.cost: Free entry; shared jeep or taxi fare, indicative
experiences.summary: Ride up the Rangeet road from Jorethang to Legship, the gateway to Gyalshing, to visit the Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple on the riverbank. Hindu tradition holds that Shiva appeared to Arjuna here as the hunter Kirateshwar. Go on a quiet morning or join the crowds at Maha Shivaratri.
body: Legship sits on the Rangeet at the foot of the climb to Gyalshing and Pelling, about an hour up the river road from Jorethang. Its name comes from Lepcha, for a fern said to taste like chilli. The Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple stands on the riverbank close to town and is one of the holiest Shiva temples in Sikkim, with smaller shrines to Rama and Durga in the same complex. It sits in Gyalshing district, just across the line from South Sikkim.

Hindu tradition holds that after Arjuna's long penance, Shiva appeared to him at this very spot as the hunter Kirateshwar and blessed him before the Kurukshetra war. The main object of worship is a natural stone lingam. Kirati people call the place Kirateshwar Mahadev Thaan. Pilgrims believe a sincere visit fulfils wishes, especially for children, health and family harmony. The biggest gatherings come at Bala Chaturdashi in November–December and Maha Shivaratri in February–March.

Shared jeeps heading to Gyalshing and Pelling pass through Legship, or hire a local taxi from Jorethang with waiting for a half day; agree the price first and check current status before you travel. Entry is free. Remove shoes, dress modestly and follow the priests' lead. Pair the temple with a look at the Rangeet dam lake at Legship, or continue up to Pelling the same day. If you go back to Jorethang, leave Legship by early afternoon, as jeeps thin out later.

faqs.q: How far is Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple from Jorethang
faqs.a: The temple is at Legship, about an hour up the Rangeet road from Jorethang by jeep or car. Shared jeeps to Gyalshing and Pelling pass through Legship, so you can hop off there. A local taxi with waiting makes it an easy half-day trip. Road conditions vary, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the legend of Kirateshwar Mahadev
faqs.a: Hindu tradition holds that Shiva appeared to the warrior Arjuna at this spot as Kirateshwar, a hunter, after Arjuna's long penance, and blessed him before the Kurukshetra war. The main object of worship is a natural stone lingam. Pilgrims believe a sincere visit fulfils wishes, especially for children and good health.

faqs.q: When are the festivals at Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple
faqs.a: The two biggest are Bala Chaturdashi in November–December and Maha Shivaratri in February–March. Both draw large crowds from Sikkim and Darjeeling, with long queues and busy roads. Dates follow the Hindu lunar calendar and change each year, so check current status before you travel and arrive early in the morning.

faqs.q: Is Jorethang worth visiting
faqs.a: As a stop, yes; as a destination, mainly in mid-January. Jorethang is the junction where Darjeeling, Namchi and Pelling roads meet, with a busy morning market, cheap food and a riverside on the Rangeet. During the Maghe Sankranti Mela, around 14 January, it is worth a night. Otherwise most people pause here for an hour.

faqs.q: How far is Jorethang from Darjeeling
faqs.a: Jorethang is ≈ 30 km from Darjeeling, about 1.5–2 hours by road down to the Rangeet. A shared jeep costs about ₹150–200 a seat, indicative for 2026. It is the usual route from Darjeeling to Pelling, Namchi and the rest of West and South Sikkim. Check current status before you travel in the monsoon.

faqs.q: How do I go from Darjeeling to Pelling by shared jeep
faqs.a: Take a shared jeep from Darjeeling to Jorethang, about ₹150–200 a seat, then another to Gyalshing or Pelling, about ₹150–250, indicative for 2026. Leave Darjeeling by 8 am, because most onward jeeps from Jorethang go before about 1 pm. From Gyalshing, short shared hops reach Pelling for about ₹50–80.

faqs.q: When is the Maghe Sankranti Mela in Jorethang
faqs.a: It starts on Maghe Sankranti, usually 14 January, and runs for about a week on the banks of the Rangeet. The 71st mela ran from 14 to 22 January 2026, according to the Sikkim government. Book rooms early, as Jorethang's few hotels fill up, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Jorethang hot
faqs.a: Yes, by Sikkim standards. At about 320 m it is far lower than Darjeeling, Namchi or Pelling, so winters are mild and April to September is hot and humid. Pack light layers for Jorethang and warm ones for the hill towns. October to March is the most comfortable time to stop here.

faqs.q: Where should I stay near Jorethang
faqs.a: Jorethang has a few simple hotels near the bazaar and jeep stand, fine for one night if you miss an onward jeep. For more comfort, go up to Namchi, ≈ 17 km and 40 minutes away, which has more hotels. For a village stay, Okhrey's Sherpa homestays are about 2 hours away on the road to Barsey.

faqs.q: Do foreigners need a permit at Jorethang
faqs.a: Yes. Foreign nationals need Sikkim's Restricted Area Permit to enter the state, including Jorethang. It is free, valid for 30 days and can be applied for online through e-FRRO; it is also issued at the Melli and Rangpo checkposts. Arrange it before you reach Jorethang and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What can I do in Jorethang in a few hours
faqs.a: Walk the morning bazaar and eat sel roti with tea, buy hard chhurpi to take home, then walk down to the Rangeet for the view. With half a day, ride up to Namchi for Samdruptse or along the river to the Kirateshwar Mahadev Temple at Legship. In mid-January, spend the evening at the mela.

faqs.q: Is the road through Jorethang open in the monsoon
faqs.a: Usually, but landslides close sections of the roads into Jorethang several times most monsoons, especially from June to September. Delays of a few hours are common and longer closures happen. Keep a spare day, travel early in the day and check current status before you travel with your driver or the local jeep stand.
